Photo of the skies over London while bombing and dog fights between the Germans and British planes during WWII

What an incredible photo. Was everyone in a constant state of panic or did they try to keep to a routine and go to work? All my Mom would ever tell me is you had to keep the lights in your house off at night so you where not a target.
My grandparents had a bomb land at the top of their street during this time. Fortunately for them it was a dud and never went off..that's about all I was told of the incident though.
Wouldn't you also have to be worried about stray bullets and plane wreckage dropping from the sky during a battle like this? Can't imagine the sounds that you would hear either.

You would usually be in a shelter during a raid so shrapnel and wreckage etc. wouldn't be an issue unless a whole plane landed on you. I remember my father telling me how after the air raids all the kids would scour the streets for bits of shrapnel or the tail fins off bombs.

There was a blackout over the whole of Britain during the Blitz. They had wardens who patrolled the streets ensuring no-one was showing lights and there were legal penalties in place for people who didn't comply.

People didn't generally panic, they just carried on with their normal lives as the air raids didn't last that long. When the sirens sounded you'd go down to the air raid shelters and wait for the all clear.
That had to have been absolutely surreal to be there in the moment.

My father was a child during WW2 and he remembers this happening. He remembers a night time air raid and standing outside watching the search lights scanning the sky. After a while one of them caught a plane in its light and then every search light in the area switched to the plane and the anti-aircraft guns started to fire on it. He said he remembers the plane trying like anything to escape the lights but there were too many following him, and eventually one of the guns got him. He said it was a very sombor moment, nobody was cheering or happy when the plane went down, and his mother kept talking about the parents of that young man who just died never seeing their son again.
